root.claim: One deterministic fixed-alphabet, fixed-tape Turing machine computes the exact $2n$-bit product of two $n$-bit integers in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ worst-case time with $\kappa=2^{-182}$, disproving the $n\log n$ conjecture in this model.
root.method: Reduce the product to radix-digit convolution, move it by a Chinese-remainder map, Gaussian resampling, chirps and a phase twist to convolution over $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ computed by synthetic transforms; speed up the transforms' address movement and butterfly layers with two network-based tape procedures; then prove exact recovery and total the costs.

motivation.text: Scanning $\Theta(n)$ stored bits at each of $\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$, so beating $n\log n$ needs savings in both data movement and arithmetic.

quote.quote:
Scanning an array of $\Theta(n)$ stored bits at each of
$\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$.
We therefore need savings in both movement and arithmetic.

children.claim: Two tape procedures save over plain scanning: address chunks of width $u$ are interchanged in $O(Vu^\tau)$ time, and a simultaneous normalized butterfly layer on $D\le d$ chunks costs $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$, with fixed $\tau,\lambda'<1$.
children.method: Build each procedure from its own fixed linear network that exchanges two banks and restores scratch wires, apply the network pointwise to row-split role streams with frames chosen so every edge is a few smaller calls, and solve the volume-normalized recurrence.

motivation.text: Because the smaller calls number $s<Wm$ and each acts on volume $V/W$, multiplying the parameter by $m$ raises normalized cost by only $s/W<m$; this strict inequality is the source of the power saving.

quote.quote:
This strict inequality
is the source of the power saving.

children.claim: Two fixed finite networks (a bit network over $\mathbb F_2$ and a complex network over $\mathbb Z[i,1/2]$) exchange two banks while restoring scratch wires, and their label budgets lose $L<N/2$, so the total number $s$ of smaller calls their edges need satisfies $s<Wm$.
children.method: Construct the three-stage bank exchange on triples of a 100-element set, label it with nested nondegenerate subspaces, and count the label-dimension changes.

motivation.text: The number of smaller operations an edge needs is its label-dimension change, so a strict deficit in the total change is exactly what yields the saving.

quote.quote:
The saving will come from keeping the total dimension lost on decreasing
edges small relative to $N$.

children.claim: A scalar linear network of $W$ wires, built from three stages of copy, gather, scatter and side-injection gates on triples, sends the two banks $(X_a,Y_a)$ to $(-Y_a,X_a)$ (a plain swap over $\mathbb F_2$) and returns every scratch wire to its arbitrary initial value.
children.method: Run an eight-row gate schedule per invocation that first subtracts the effect of the old scratch values, then injects $x$ into $y$ and finally undoes its own auxiliary updates; compose a forward, an inverse and a forward invocation over the three triple coordinates.

motivation.text: Subtracting the old scratch contribution before using the scratch wires makes the net effect independent of their arbitrary initial values, and three add/subtract stages $y\gets y+x$, $x\gets x-y$, $y\gets y+x$ realize an exchange of banks.

quote.quote:
The first two rows of
the following schedule remove the effect of the old scratch values;
the next four introduce the source values and add their effect to the
target; the last two restore the scratch values.

children.claim: For arbitrary initial scratch values a forward invocation adds $x_S$ to $y_S$ and changes nothing else, because the central coefficient ($|S\cap T|\bmod 2$, or $(|S\cap T|-1)/2$) and the side coefficient cancel for all neighbouring distinct triples.

quote.quote:
For arbitrary initial values of its auxiliary wires, a forward
invocation changes $y_S$ to $y_S+x_S$ and leaves every other value
unchanged.

children.claim: Forward, inverse and forward invocations at stages 1, 2, 3 take $(x,y)$ to $(x,y+x)$, then $(-y,y+x)$, then $(-y,x)$.

quote.quote:
Starting from $(x,y)$, the three stages give
$(x,y+x)$, then $(-y,y+x)$, then $(-y,x)$.

children.claim: Every gate and terminal of either network can be labelled by a nondegenerate subspace of the $m$-dimensional space $\mathcal F=F^{\otimes3}$ so that labels are nested along every edge and the only decreasing edges are the central-wire edges from time 3 to time 4, each losing dimension $h$; hence the absolute label changes sum to $Wm-2N+2L$ with $L=Ich$.
children.method: Pair triple indicator vectors by a form under which neighbouring triples are orthogonal, expose one tensor factor per stage with prescribed incoming and outgoing labels, and assign common gate labels by the decomposition $A\otimes F=(B\otimes F)\perp(P\otimes F)$.

motivation.text: Because neighbouring triple lines are orthogonal, a side wire's label can grow through $P\otimes\langle t_X\rangle\subset P\otimes t_Y^\perp$ without ever shrinking, so all loss of dimension is confined to the single return of each central wire.

children.claim: With the rational form $x^{\mathsf T}(I-J/9)y$ (bit network) or the binary dot product (complex network), every triple line is nondegenerate and neighbouring triple lines are orthogonal.

quote.quote:
Thus every triple line is nondegenerate, and neighboring triple lines
are orthogonal, in the label field belonging to either construction.

children.claim: The stage transitions expose one tensor factor at each stage, and the outgoing labels of one stage are exactly the incoming labels of the next, starting at $U_a$ on $X_a$ and ending at $U_a^\perp$ on $Y_a$.

quote.quote: These transitions expose one tensor factor at each stage.

children.claim: Every edge joins comparable nondegenerate labels, the only decreasing edges are central-wire edges from time 3 to time 4 with loss $h$, and in the binary label space every nonzero residual has an orthonormal basis.

quote.quote:
Every edge joins comparable nondegenerate labels.  The only decreasing
edges are the central-wire edges from time 3 to time 4; their dimension
loss is $h$.

children.claim: The loss ratios are $L_{\rm b}/N=100/539$ and $L_{\rm c}/N=101/539$, both smaller than $1/2$.

quote.quote: In particular, both are smaller than $1/2$.

children.salient: Both networks lose strictly less than half of the $N$ data dimensions, which is what leaves room for the extra source ranks and still gives $s<Wm$.
The networks must move every one of the $W$ roles, yet the total count $s$ of smaller calls stays strictly below $Wm$; this strict inequality is the only source of the power saving.

adds.name: data pairs
adds.meaning: The number of index triples $a\in\mathcal T^3$, i.e. the number of wires in each data bank.

adds.name: lost dimension
adds.meaning: The total dimension lost on decreasing edges of the labelled network.

adds.name: ground-set size
adds.meaning: The size $h=100$ of the ground set whose 3-element subsets index the banks.

children.claim: The fast address-chunk interchange: one fixed procedure interchanges two disjoint $u$-bit address fields of any array in $O(Vu^\tau)$ time with $\tau=1-2^{-50}$.
children.method: Prove the power-width case with enough rows first, then supply rows from the top digits of the chunks, split a general width into base-$m$ pieces, and pad binary chunks to radix-$q$ ranges.

motivation.text: A few high digits of the chunks themselves supply the rows the power-width case needs, and moving them costs less than the final bound.

quote.quote:
Rows for a general array can be supplied by a few of its own high digits.
Their movement will cost less than the final bound.

children.claim: For $e=m^k$, two disjoint chunks of $e$ radix-$q$ digits, preceded by a row field whose length is divisible by $W^k$, can be interchanged in $O(Ve^\tau)$ time on fixed tapes.
children.method: Split rows cyclically among the $W$ roles of the bit network, use shear frames $\Phi_M$ so the network computes $H\gets H+D$ on every role, implement each edge by recursive smaller interchanges, finish the interchange with two linear updates, and solve the volume-normalized recurrence.

motivation.text: Each edge of rank $a$ costs $a$ smaller interchanges on streams of volume $V/W$, and the ranks sum to $s<Wm$, so multiplying the width by $m$ multiplies normalized cost by only $s/W<m^\tau$.

quote.quote:
An edge matrix of rank $a$ will require $a$ smaller interchanges.
Because the sum of these ranks is less than the number of wires times
$m$, the resulting recurrence saves a power of the chunk width.

children.claim: Assigning the projection $P_U$ to each vertex with label $U$ (and $-P_{U_a}$ to source $X_a$) gives fixed rational matrices with $M_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}-M_{\mathrm{source}(w)}=I_m$ on every role and edge ranks summing to $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}m-N+2L_{\rm b}<W_{\rm b}m$.
children.method: Use projections onto the nested labels as frame matrices; the rank of a difference of nested projections is the label-dimension change, and the negative source projection adds one rank per data pair.

motivation.text: Frames $\Phi_M$ compose additively in $M$, so an edge needs a shear by the matrix difference, whose rank is the number of smaller interchanges; projections make that rank equal to the label residual counted in the budget.

children.claim: For nested nondegenerate $U\subset V$, $P_V-P_U$ is the projection onto $V\cap U^\perp$, so its rank is $\dim V-\dim U$.

quote.quote:
For $U\subset V$ nondegenerate,
$P_V-P_U$ is the identity on $V\cap U^\perp$ and zero on its
orthogonal complement.

children.claim: On $X_a$ the endpoint difference is $P_{U_a^\perp}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m$, and every other role has zero source and identity sink matrix.

quote.quote:
For an input $X_a$ the endpoint difference is
$P_{U_a^\perp}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m$.

children.claim: The relative rank deficits exceed $20\cdot2^{-50}$, so $s_{\rm b}/W_{\rm b}<m^\tau$ (and $s_{\rm c}/W_{\rm c}<m^\sigma$) with $\tau=\sigma=1-2^{-50}$.

quote.quote: Both exact deficits displayed above are greater than $20\cdot2^{-50}$.

children.claim: For a fixed rational $m\times m$ matrix $A$ of rank $a$, the shear $(H,D)\mapsto(H+AD,D)$ over $\mathbb Z/q^b\mathbb Z$ takes exactly $a$ interchanges of $b$-digit fields plus $O(V)$ work.
children.method: Factor $A=E_1\Pi E_2$ with lower triangular $E_1,E_2$, apply the triangular factors by controlled shifts, and realize each one of $\Pi$ by add, interchange, subtract.

motivation.text: Controlled shifts update a later field from earlier ones in linear time, and lower triangular coordinate changes only ever need that direction, so only the $a$ ones of $\Pi$ need a costly interchange.

quote.quote:
updates a later field using
earlier fields in linear time.  Lower triangular changes of coordinates
can be performed entirely in this direction.

children.claim: Every rational $m\times m$ matrix of rank $a$ factors as $E_1\Pi E_2$ with $E_1,E_2$ invertible lower triangular and $\Pi$ a partial permutation with exactly $a$ ones.

quote.quote: Every rational $m\times m$ matrix $A$ of rank $a$ has a factorization

children.claim: A lower triangular transformation of $H$ or of $D$ costs $O(V)$ by updating coordinates in descending physical order.

quote.quote:
A lower triangular transformation of $H$, or of $D$, costs $O(V)$:
update coordinates in descending physical order.

children.claim: Each one of $\Pi$ is realized as $D_j\gets D_j+H_i$, $(H_i,D_j)\gets(D_j,H_i)$, $D_j\gets H_i-D_j$, using a single interchange.

quote.quote:
On an initial pair $(h,d)$ this sequence yields $(h+d,d)$.
It uses just one interchange.

children.claim: On the row-split role streams with frames $\Phi_{M_v}$, the common-frame identity and $M_{\rm out}-M_{\rm in}=I_m$ give $H\gets H+D$ on every original row, including scratch rows with arbitrary initial values.

quote.quote:
The result
is $H\leftarrow H+D$ on every original row, including rows assigned
to scratch roles, whose initial values were arbitrary.

children.claim: The updates $D\gets D-H$, $H\gets H+D$, $D\gets H-D$ send $(H,D)$ to $(D,H)$, and only the middle shear uses the network.

quote.quote:
The transformation
sends $(H,D)$ to $(D,H)$.

children.claim: With $F_k$ the time divided by volume, $F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)$, and $s/W<m^\tau$ gives $F_k=O(e^\tau)$.

quote.quote: Hence $F_k=O(e^\tau)$.

children.claim: The recursion runs on one fixed set of tapes with only $O(V)$ extra work per node, for every depth and every spectator length.
children.method: Before each child call park the $W-1$ inactive role streams on a stack tape and the descriptor on a descriptor stack, reuse the same role and work tapes in the child, and restore afterwards.

motivation.text: A fixed machine cannot allocate new tapes per recursion depth, and parking costs only the node's own volume, so the recurrence's factor $s/W$ is not spoiled by temporary storage.

quote.quote:
Temporary storage is
therefore not substituted for logical volume in the factor $s/W$.

children.claim: Before a recursive call the $W-1$ inactive role streams are appended to the parking stack, the active stream is copied to the child area, and they are popped back on return.

quote.quote:
Before a recursive call, append the $W-1$ inactive role streams to the
parking stack in a fixed order, with separators.

children.claim: Every push, pop, copy, positioning or erasure moves $O(V)$ symbols at a parent with $s$ children, giving exactly the additional $O(V)$ term.

quote.quote:
Each push, pop, copy, positioning operation, or erasure moves $O(V)$
symbols at a parent node.

children.claim: Descriptor work is $(\log(2V_0))^{O(1)}=O(V_j)$ at every depth, so one finite machine serves every depth and spectator length.

quote.quote:
These observations establish one finite machine for every recursion
depth and every choice of spectator lengths.

children.claim: After interchanging and joining the top $\rho$ digits of each chunk, those digits form a row field of range $q^{2\rho}\ge W^k$ before both remaining chunks, padded to a multiple of $W^k$ at less than twice the volume.

quote.quote: In the two middle orders, the first two fields form a row field of range

children.claim: Writing the remaining width in base $m$ and applying the power-width interchange to each piece costs $O(V)\sum_j a_jm^{j\tau}=O(Ve^\tau)$.

quote.quote:
The fixed bound $a_j<m$ and the inequality $m^k<me$ make this a
geometric sum of the stated order.

children.claim: Padding $[2^u]$ to $[q^e]$ changes the volume by a fixed factor and $e=O(u)$, so the bound is $O(Vu^\tau)$.

quote.quote:
Since $e=O(u)$ for fixed $q$, the bound is
$O(Vu^\tau)$.

children.salient: A pure permutation of addresses is done faster than $u$ passes over the data, by computing XOR combinations of data that cancel out by the end.

adds.name: chunk width
adds.meaning: The number of address bits in each of the two chunks being interchanged.

adds.name: digit width
adds.meaning: The number of radix-$q$ digits in each chunk handled by one recursive interchange.

adds.name: fixed prime radix
adds.meaning: A fixed odd prime avoiding all denominators of the network's matrices, used as the digit radix.

children.claim: The simultaneous butterfly layer: on an array of polynomial records with $D\le d$ consecutive $K$-bit chunks, $H_0$ applied to one common bit position of every chunk, followed by truncation $Q_p$, is computed in $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ time with error below $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$.
children.method: Write $H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D$, compute $C^{\otimes D}$ recursively with the complex network, keep every intermediate value exact in a guarded fixed-point format, and truncate once at the end.

motivation.text: Separate butterfly factors would need $D$ whole-array passes, whereas the network recursion gives a power saving in $d$.

quote.quote:
whereas separate butterfly
factors would require $D$ whole-array passes.

children.claim: The tensor product $C^{\otimes D}$ of the kernel $C$ on the selected bits of $D\le d$ chunks is computed exactly in $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ time, by recursion in which a group of $e$ selected axes uses $s_{\rm c}$ children on $e/m$ axes, each on a stream of volume $V/W$.
children.method: Run the complex network on row-split role streams with column phase frames, implement each edge's frame change by a binary change of basis (packed row additions) and one recursive $C^{\otimes e/m}$ call per residual vector, and unroll the volume-normalized recurrence.

motivation.text: Phase frames express a $C$ tensor product through smaller groups of selected bits separated by binary changes of basis, so the rank deficit $s<Wm$ becomes a power saving in $d$.

quote.quote:
Its phase
frames express a $C$ tensor product using smaller groups of
selected bits, separated by binary changes of basis.

children.claim: With phase frames $\mathcal C_U=H^{\otimes m}\operatorname{diag}(i^{q_U(x)})H^{\otimes m}$, each edge's frame change of the complex network is a product of one translation kernel $aI+bX_v$ (or its inverse) per orthonormal residual vector, these total $s_{\rm c}=W_{\rm c}m-2N+2L_{\rm c}<W_{\rm c}m$, and after diagonal corrections every role receives $C^{\otimes m}$.
children.method: Use weight additivity modulo four for orthogonal binary vectors to split each frame change into one phase per residual basis vector, conjugate by Hadamard matrices to turn each phase into a translation kernel, and fix the $X_a\to Y_a$ route with $Z$ signs.

motivation.text: All phase frames are diagonalized by the same $H^{\otimes m}$, so frame changes are diagonal phases, and an orthonormal residual basis splits such a phase into independent one-direction factors, each one smaller $C$ layer.

children.claim: If $z\cdot w=0$ over $\mathbb F_2$, then $\operatorname{wt}(z+w)\equiv\operatorname{wt}(z)+\operatorname{wt}(w)\pmod 4$, so $q_V-q_U$ is a sum of one term per orthonormal residual vector.

quote.quote:
If $z\cdot w=0$, the intersection cardinality is even, so weight is
additive modulo four.

children.claim: Each such phase $i^{\pm[v\cdot x]}$ becomes, after Hadamard conjugation, the kernel $aI+bX_v$ or its inverse.

quote.quote:
The displayed phase therefore
becomes $aI+bX_v$ or its inverse.

children.claim: Applying $Z$ signs on the 27 support coordinates and the scalar $i^{27k}$ turns the $X_a\to Y_a$ route into $C^{\otimes mk}$ as well.

quote.quote:
The operator
on this pair is therefore $C^{\otimes mk}$ as well.

children.claim: Conjugating by an address permutation $\mathcal P_M$ whose first columns are the residual basis turns each directional kernel into $C^{\pm1}$ on coordinate slot $h$, i.e. one child operation on the $f$ axes of that slot.

quote.quote:
This is one child operation
on the $f$ axes in slot $h$.

children.claim: An inverse kernel needs only one forward child, since $(C^{-1})^{\otimes f}=(-i)^fZ^{\otimes f}C^{\otimes f}Z^{\otimes f}$.

quote.quote:
A negative directional kernel still requires only one
forward child, because

children.claim: The change of basis $\mathcal P_M$ is a fixed number of row additions, each XORing corresponding selected positions of two whole slots.

quote.quote:
Thus one row addition changes corresponding selected
positions in two whole slots.

children.claim: Applying the network with these column frames to $e=mf$ selected axes gives exactly $s_{\rm c}$ child calls, each on the $f=e/m$ axes of one slot, and yields $C^{\otimes e}$ on every role.

quote.quote:
Summing its residual dimensions gives exactly
$s_{\rm c}$ child calls, each on the $f=e/m$ axes of one slot.

children.claim: For three $L$-bit chunks $x,y,z$ with $L=fK$, the XORs $y_{j_i}\gets y_{j_i}\oplus x_{j_i}$ at positions $j_i=\rho+iK$ are performed while restoring $z$, in time $O(V(L^\tau+1))$ under the layer's parameter growth.
children.method: Use eight packed cyclic shifts of whole chunk ranges, each controlled by $x$ and guarded by parities of $z$, which flip the selected parities segment by segment, then correct the small address-determined set where guards overflow by extracting and radix-sorting those records.

motivation.text: The correction depends only on addresses, so the time bound is worst-case over all payloads; and the exceptional set is so small that sorting it costs $o(V)$.

quote.quote:
The correction depends only on addresses, so the time bound is
worst-case over all payloads.

children.claim: The eight conditional updates flip the parity of $u$ exactly when $c=1$, preserve both quotients by two and restore the auxiliary integer $w$.

quote.quote:
Thus the parity of $u$
is flipped precisely when $c=1$, both quotients under division by two are
preserved, and the arbitrary auxiliary integer $w$ is restored.

children.claim: By the union bound over the $2(f-1)$ guards, the exceptional set satisfies $|\mathcal B|\le\delta_{\rm bad}M$ with $\delta_{\rm bad}=\min\{1,80(f-1)2^{-K}\}$.

quote.quote: the union bound over the $2(f-1)$ guards gives

children.claim: The packed shifts $S_0$ and the ideal map $T_0$ agree off $\mathcal B$, so $T_0S_0^{-1}$ fixes the complement of $\mathcal B$ and permutes $\mathcal B$.

quote.quote: Thus $T_0S_0^{-1}$ fixes $\mathcal B^c$ and permutes $\mathcal B$.

children.claim: Extracting the exceptional records with destination ranks, radix-sorting them and reinserting them implements $T_0$ everywhere.

quote.quote: This implements $T_0$ everywhere.

children.claim: Each binary change of basis and its inverse cost $O(V((eK)^\tau+1))$ on a stream of volume $V$.

quote.quote:
the complete change of basis and its inverse therefore cost
$O(V((eK)^\tau+1))$ on a stream of volume $V$.

children.claim: Applying $C$ individually to the first $q_0$ chunks lets their bits serve as a row index of range at least $W^{k_0}$, padded to a multiple of $W^{k_0}$.

quote.quote:
Otherwise apply \(C\) individually on the selected bits of the first
\(q_0\) chunks, in \(O(V\log d)\) time.

children.claim: The normalized cost satisfies $F(e)\le(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^\tau+1)$, because the $s$ children run on streams of volume $V/W$.

quote.quote:
Dividing by
the current volume \(V\) gives the factor \(s/W\).

children.claim: Summing over the base-$m$ pieces and the row preprocessing gives normalized cost $O(d^{\lambda'})$ for $\max\{\lambda,\sigma+\beta(1-\sigma)\}<\lambda'<1$.

quote.quote: Adding their costs and the row preprocessing gives

children.claim: Every chain of arithmetic in one layer has length below $C_0d^{C_1}$, so reserving $p+\Delta$ fractional and $\Delta+3$ integer bits ($\Delta=o(p)$) keeps every intermediate coefficient exact.

quote.quote:
Thus reserving \(p+\Delta\)
fractional bits and \(\Delta+3\) integer and sign bits per real
component represents every intermediate coefficient exactly and
prevents overflow.

children.claim: The identity $H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D$ converts the exact $C$ layer into the normalized layer $\mathcal H$.

quote.quote: converts the resulting exact $C$-layer to $\mathcal H$.

children.claim: $\mathcal H$ maps disk arrays to disk arrays, and the single final truncation keeps the disk with error below $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$.

quote.quote:
Thus $\mathcal H$ maps disk arrays to disk
arrays, and componentwise truncation preserves that disk and has
error less than $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$

children.salient: The cost grows only like $d^{\lambda'}$ with $\lambda'<1$: applying butterflies on $d$ axes at once is cheaper than $d$ separate passes.

adds.name: active chunks
adds.meaning: The number of consecutive $K$-bit address chunks whose selected bit the layer acts on.

adds.name: chunk width
adds.meaning: The number of address bits in each chunk, $K=\lfloor d^c\rfloor$.

adds.name: two-point kernel
adds.meaning: The Gaussian-dyadic $2\times2$ matrix $aI+bX$ that the complex network applies on every role.

adds.name: label dimension
adds.meaning: The dimension $m=h^3=10^6$ of the label space, i.e. the factor by which the parameter shrinks per recursion level.

adds.name: wire count
adds.meaning: The number of wires (roles) of a finite network, including scratch wires.

adds.name: smaller calls
adds.meaning: The total number of smaller recursive calls needed over all edges of a network.

adds.name: interchange exponent
adds.meaning: The fixed exponent $1-2^{-50}$ in the interchange cost $O(Vu^\tau)$.

adds.name: layer exponent
adds.meaning: The fixed exponent $1-2^{-54}$ in the butterfly-layer cost $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$.

children.claim: Normalized cyclic convolution $\mathcal M_r(f,g)=(f*g)/T$ of disk-grid arrays over $\mathcal R_r=\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ is approximated with error below $\sqrt2M(3\ell+1)2^{-p}$ at cost $O(Tp[dK+pK^{\tau-1}+\ell d^{\lambda'}+\log(rp)])$.
children.method: Apply two forward synthetic transforms, multiply the records pointwise in their retained stored order by signed packing, apply one opposite transform consuming that order, and scale exactly by $M$.

motivation.text: Pointwise multiplication commutes with applying the same record permutation to both operands, so the stored frequency order never has to be undone between the forward and opposite transforms.

quote.quote:
Pointwise multiplication commutes with applying the same record
permutation $LB$ to both operands.

children.claim: On $d-1$ power-of-two axes of length $2^{\ell}$ or $2^{\ell-1}$ over $\mathcal R_r$, the forward synthetic transform $LBF_{\boldsymbol t}^-$ and its opposite $F_{\boldsymbol t}^+B^{-1}L^{-1}$ are computed with error below $\sqrt2\ell\,2^{-p}$ at cost $O(Tp[dK+pK^{\tau-1}+\ell d^{\lambda'}])$.
children.method: Use decimation-in-frequency rounds of $H_0$ butterflies and monomial twiddles, leaving outputs in bit-reversed order; move bit slots so each round's selected bits sit at a common offset in consecutive $K$-bit chunks; run each round with the simultaneous layer and truncate once per round.

motivation.text: The simultaneous layer applies only when the participating axes' selected bits sit at a common offset in consecutive $K$-bit chunks, so the layout must be built first.

quote.quote:
To apply Proposition~\ref{prop:simultaneous-layer} in a transform round,
we must place the selected bits of the participating axes at a common
offset in consecutive $K$-bit chunks.

children.claim: The decimation-in-frequency recursion with monomial twiddles computes $F_t^-$ and stores entry $j$ at bit-reversed slot $\operatorname{rev}_a(j)$.

quote.quote: entry $(F_t^-z)_j$ occupies slot $\operatorname{rev}_a(j)$.

children.claim: Running the recursion in reverse implements the opposite transform $F_t^+B_t^{-1}$ directly on the stored order.

quote.quote:
Thus the two
exact procedures implement

children.claim: On several axes the steps of one round group into a parallel butterfly $\mathcal H$ followed by one recordwise monomial $J_E$.

quote.quote:
Consequently the individual axis steps may be grouped as a parallel
butterfly $\mathcal H$, followed by one recordwise monomial operation
$J_E$.

children.claim: The layout $L$ uses at most $Dq-1$ chunk exchanges of width $K$, costing $O(Tp\,pK^{\tau-1})$.

quote.quote:
This uses at most $Dq-1$
exchanges of width-$K$ address chunks, even when the chunks are
nonadjacent.

children.claim: Each round runs the simultaneous layer at cost $O(Tpd^{\lambda'})$, for $O(Tp\ell d^{\lambda'})$ in total.

quote.quote:
The simultaneous-layer procedure therefore applies at cost
$O(Tpd^{\lambda'})$ per round and $O(Tp\ell d^{\lambda'})$ in total.

children.claim: Because truncation commutes with the signed coefficient permutation $J_E$, each round equals one truncation after an exact contraction, so errors add to below $\sqrt2\ell\,2^{-p}$.

quote.quote:
Thus the actual forward call sequence returns exactly the result of
truncating once after the exact contraction round.

children.claim: For disk-grid polynomials $f,g\in\mathcal R_r$, the normalized product $Q_p(fg/r)$ is computed exactly up to its final truncation in $O(rp\log(rp))$ time on fixed tapes.
children.method: Evaluate the signed integer coefficient polynomials at $B_0=2^{4p}$, multiply four pairs with the established $O(N\log N)$ multiplier, extract centered coefficients block by block, fold modulo $y^r+1$ and truncate.

motivation.text: Kronecker substitution turns all coefficient products into a few long integer products, which the established multiplier does fast; blocks of $4p$ bits exceed twice every product coefficient, so centered residues recover the signed coefficients exactly.

children.claim: Each signed evaluation $A_u=u(B_0)$ has magnitude below $B_0^r/2$ and fits in $4pr$ bits.

quote.quote: shows that each magnitude fits in $4pr$ bits.
